FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 13 February 1989, after the 
draft finalized by the Small Tools Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineer- 
ing Division Council. 

In the preparation of this standard, considerable assistance has been derived from DIN 1825 : 1977 
'Pinion type cutters for cylindrical gears; disc gear cutters for spur gears', issued by the Deutsches Institut 
fiir Normung ( DIN ). 



Itl2SMt 19t» 



Indian Standard 



SMALL TOOLS — 
GEAR SHAPER CUTTERS 



PISC TYPE 
- SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard covers the dimensions and 
other requirements of disc type gear shaper cutters 
suitable for module 1 to 12> conforming to 
IS 2535 : 1978 'Basic rack and modules of 
cylindrical gears for general engineering and 
heavy engineering ( second revision )\ 



2 REFERENCES 

ISJVo. 

IS 2102 

(Part 1) : 1980 



Title 

General tolerances for 
dimensions and form and 
position: Part 1 General 
tolerances for linear and 
angular dimensions {second 
revision ) 

Specification for high speed 
tool steel ( first revision ) 

Methods for sampling small 
tools 

Technical supply conditions 
for general purpose gear 
hobs 



IS 7291 : 1981 
IS 7778 : 1975 
IS 8731 : 1978 

3 DIMENSIONS 

3*1 Dimensions of disc type gear shaper cutter 
shall be as given in Tables 1 to 5, read with 
Fig. 1. 

3.2 Tolerances 

3.2.1 Glass of accuracy and tolerance of cutters 
shall be according to Indian Standard Gear 
shaper cutter — Glass of accuracy and tolerance 

( under preparation )', 



NOiTE — Till such time the standard under prepara- 
tion! is published, the requirement shall be as agreed 
to between the purchaser and the supplier. 

3.2.2 For dimensions where tolerance has not 
been specified, tolerance of medium series of 
IS 2102 ( Part 1 ) : 1980 shall apply. 

4 MATERIAL 

4.1 Gear shaper cutter shall be of high speed tool 
steel Off designation XT 91 W6 GoMo5Cr4V2 in 
accordance with IS 7291 : 1981 or equivalent, as 
agreed to between the manufacturer and the user. 

5 HAIUINESS 

5.1 Depending upon the choice of the high speed 
steel, hardness shall be between 820 to 900 HV 
measured on a flat surface. 

6 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 

6.1 All sharp corners except cuttmg edges shall 
be removed. 

6.2 Profile of gear shaper cutter shall be accord- 
ing to 'Indian Stardard Reference profile for 
gear cutting tools for involute teeth according to 
IS 2535 : 1978 ( under preparation )\ 

NOTE — Till such time the standard on profile of 
gear ihaper cutters is published, IS 8731 t 1978 shall be 
referred. 

6.3 For the requirements not covered under this 
standard, reference shall be made to Indian 
Standard Gear shaper cutter — Technical supply 
conditions ( under preparation )\ 

NOTE — Till such time the standard under prepara- 
tion is published, the requirement shall be as agreed 
to between the purchaser and the supplier.

1 PROTECTIVE COATING 

Each gear shaper cutter shall be covered by a 
suitable rust proofing material and then vsrrappcd 
in non-absorbent paper. 

^ SAMPLING 

The sampling and criteria of acceptance shall be 
in accordance with IS 7778 : 1975. 

9 DESIGNATION 

A disc type spur gear shaper cutter with module 
2-5 mm, nominal pitch diameter 100 mm, bore- 
hole 44 mm, Glass of accuracy * A' and reference 
profile RPI shall be designated as: 

Disc Type Gear Shaper Cutter 

2-5 X 100 X 44 X A — RPI — IS : 12536 



10 MARKING 



Gear shaper cutter shall be marked with the 
foUowibig information: 

a) pcsignation 

b) Module 

c) pressure angle 

d) Number of teeth 
c) Reference profile 

f ) Working depth 

g) Name or trade mark of manufacturer 

11 PACKING AND PACKAGING 

Each gear shaper cutter or a number of gear 
shaper cutters of ssune type shall be packed in a 
carton: bearing the size, number, designation, 
manufacturer's name and trade mark.

Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards 
Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products 
covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply 
with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and 
quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard 
marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a 
further safeguard. Details of oondiilons under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark 
may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of 
Indian Standards.
